title: Harvey Weinstein Sentenced to 15 Years in Prison for Sexual Assault After New York Retrial
description:
Harvey Weinstein was sentenced Wednesday to 15 years in prison for sexually assaulting former production assistant Miriam Haley in 2006. 

	After an
body:
Harvey Weinstein was sentenced Wednesday to 15 years in prison for sexually assaulting former production assistant Miriam Haley in 2006. 

	After an overturned conviction and two subsequent mistrials, the sentencing marks a major endpoint in the New York chapter of the nine-year courtroom saga that ignited the global #MeToo movement. Barring another successful appeal, Weinstein will remain behind bars under his new New York sentence. 
	

	Next, Weinstein will face resentencing in California for raping and sexually assaulting Italian model and actor Evgeniya Chernyshova at a Los Angeles hotel in 2013. Judge Curtis Farber says it’s up to the state of California to determine whether its sentencing will run concurrent or consecutively. No date has been set.


	In an emotional witness impact statement, Haley said she “certainly didn’t think I’d be standing here again six years after the [first] conviction” and “trusts it will be my final one.” She detailed the “draining and unpleasant process” of testifying in court that came paired with “belitting cross-examination” as well as “being harassed and threatened online.”“It has often felt like I was the one on trial,” Haley lamented. “This process has been the worst decision of my life, for me personally. I considered pulling out so many times.”Haley has now testified against Weinstein at two trials, first helping secure his 2020 conviction before it was overturned four years later. She returned to the witness stand at his 2025 retrial, once again recounting how Weinstein forcibly performed oral sex on her at his SoHo apartment on July 10, 2006. A jury ultimately convicted Weinstein of committing a first-degree criminal sexual act against Haley.

	The disgraced Hollywood producer, 74, has faced a series of health issues in recent years, including chronic myeloid leukemia, diabetes and significant mobility problems. The sentence all but guarantees that Weinstein will spend the rest of his life behind bars.

	In a final statement, assistant District Attorney Nicole Blumberg asked Judge Curtis Farber for a 20-year sentence, plus five years of post-release supervision. Blumberg argued that 20 years “is the only appropriate punishment” because Weinstein “hasn’t shown an ounce of remorse” and continued “to engage in public and unrelenting victim shaming,” referring to his 2025 podcast interview with Candace Owens which she notes are laden with “conspiracies.”

schema.headline: Harvey Weinstein Sentenced to 15 Years in Prison for Sexual Assault After New York Retrial

title: Bad Brains’ Earliest Studio Recordings to Be Released in November
description: As anyone reading this probably knows, the Bad Brains were one of the most important punk-rock bands of all time, Washington D.C.-bred pioneers of t
body:
As anyone reading this probably knows, the Bad Brains were one of the most important punk-rock bands of all time, Washington D.C.-bred pioneers of the sound that became hardcore. While they were a complete anomaly at the time — four Black dudes in an overwhelmingly white music scene who seasoned their blistering rock songs with impressively authentic reggae — their impact was immediate and immense. 

	They are considered by many to be the greatest hardcore band of all time; Dave Grohl has said he learned how to play drums by bashing on pillows along with their records, and a mural of the band was painted in 2024 across the street from the site of their frequent haunt CBGB in New York. While the group was as fractious interpersonally as they were musically — they split up many times, usually when they were on the verge of a breakthrough — their early albums and particularly their explosive live shows contain some of the most powerful rock music of the ‘80s. 
	



	

					 (Photo by Al Pereira/Michael Ochs Archives/Getty Images)
									Getty Images
	



	The group’s catalog is about to get an addition that is both old and new: On November 6, just in time to join the insurrection that will surely follow the midterm elections, a little-known recording of their first session in a proper studio will be released as “Are You Ready: The First Studio Recordings” via Trust Recordings. While an early demo recording was release in 1996 as the “Black Dots” album, this six-song session, recorded in an hour at Inner Ear Studios in March 1979, predates even that by three months.


	The recordings were remixed by Minor Threat/ Fugazi co-founder and longtime friend Ian MacKaye — who has been on an archival binge recently, having worked with Henry Rollins to restore the catalog of psychobilly legends the Cramps — and will be available on vinyl, cassette, and digital. The EP joins the group’s full catalog, much of which was out of circulation for many years but recently got a proper reissue treatment and now is available on streaming services.
	

	It includes a previously unreleased recording of the band’s legendary debut single, “Pay to Cum,” which is released today with video footage filmed ay CBGB in October of 1979.



	“The riff for ‘Pay to Cum’ started as a stream of punk rock vibes fueled by the Ramones, the Damned, and Return to Forever,” says Bad Brains bassist Darryl Jenifer, reflecting the band’s unusual combination of inlfuences. “It was a gift that served as a springboard into our sound – sheer, straight-ahead three-chord mayhem with a few breaks and a stop. The title actually meant nothing to us; it was just a fun-loving play on words.” Listen/share “Pay to Cum” here and watch the video – with footage was filmed by Barry Masterson at CBGB’s October 24th 1979.

	On November 5, a day before the album’s release, Jenifer and Ian will appear in conversation at the Martin Luther King Jr. Memorial Library, discussing the session and the band’s formative years. From November 6 through the 22nd, an exhibition of archival Bad Brains material will open, featuring contributions from the archives of Darryl Jenifer, Alison Braun, BJ Papas, Lucien Perkins, Alec MacKaye, Roger Gastman, and more.

schema.headline: Bad Brains’ Earliest Studio Recordings to Be Released in November

title: Trump Rages at CNN’s Kaitlan Collins in Midnight Rant: She Has ‘Trump Addiction’
description: President Donald Trump on Tuesday night was still extremely irate that CNN‘s Kaitlan Collins tried to ask him a question at the United Nations — aft
body:
President Donald Trump on Tuesday night was still extremely irate that CNN‘s Kaitlan Collins tried to ask him a question at the United Nations — after he had banned CNN (and MS NOW and Politico) from White House coverage.

	In a post on his Truth Social platform just before midnight Tuesday, Trump accused the CNN anchor of having a “‘TRUMP’ addiction.”

	The U.S. president wrote: “All of the SLEAZEBAGS, like Third Rate ‘Reporter,’ Kaitlan Collins, of Fake News CNN, a truly unhappy person, said they weren’t going to be covering me. Then why were they ranting and raving like Lunatics, in the Press Area, at the United Nations? Why was she there? She’s got a ‘TRUMP’ addiction, and so does CNN and MSDNC. They’re all sick, treasonous, and demented! The ‘good news’ is that they have a great, for them, and totally disloyal Judge. MAKE AMERICA GREAT AGAIN! President DONALD J. TRUMP”
	

	Collins was at the UN to cover the president because that’s part of her job as CNN’s chief White House correspondent.

	On Tuesday morning, Collins asked the president a question about Americans’ sentiment that the U.S. is not winning the war with Iran, based on new CNN polling numbers. The exchange occurred outside UN headquarters in New York, prior to Trump’s remarks to the general assembly. When Trump noticed Collins, he said, “I’m surprised that CNN is here covering me. You shouldn’t be here!” Collins replied, “The United Nations allowed us in, sir.”

	Trump chastised Collins: “You should not be here covering me. You said you weren’t going to cover me. You shouldn’t be covering me.”
	

	Trump announced last Friday (Sept. 18) that he was banning CNN, MS NOW and Politico “effective immediately” from the White House because, as he has claimed hundreds of times before about media outlets he doesn’t like, they are “fake news.”

	On Monday, CNN, MS NOW and Politico sued Trump and three White House officials over his ban, alleging it violates the First Amendment and “brazenly discriminates based on editorial viewpoint.” Also Monday, in response to Trump’s ban of the news outlets, ABC News, CBS News, NBC News and Fox News — which alongside CNN provide the White House TV pool coverage — announced they were suspending coverage of the president at events because of his ban on the news outlets.

	The White House TV pool consortium, which is currently chaired by Fox News Washington bureau chief Bryan Boughton, continued to be suspended Wednesday (when NBC News was scheduled to be the pooler).

	In a court filing late Tuesday, the White House — represented by the Justice Department lawyers — responded to the lawsuit, defending the president’s ban of the news orgs. “Access to the White House is a privilege — not a right,” the administration’s filing said. It also claimed that the denial of access is a “preliminary matter” and the news organizations can contest the decision until Friday.

	Trump’s reference to the “totally disloyal Judge” in the case was to U.S. District Judge Timothy Kelly, who was nominated to the post in 2017 by Trump. Kelly will preside over an emergency hearing Wednesday to consider the media orgs’ request for a temporary restraining order to force the White House to reinstate their access.

	The White House’s filing alleged CNN, MS NOW and Politico “exhibited behavior in violation of the standards of professionalism and decorum expected of those given access to the White House Complex, including by trafficking in verifiable falsehoods about national security and other issues, and publishing sensitive or classified information.”

	As an example of CNN’s alleged infractions, the White House filing cited a Jan. 16, 2026, report that “disclosed ‘top-secret’ construction details related to the East Wing bunker, which is designed to protect the President in times of crisis or national security emergency.” Regarding MS NOW, the filing cited a June 8 story citing an anonymous White House official saying that Trump “underestimated the willingness of Iran to resume conflict.” (The filing did not specifically dispute the accuracy of the reports.)
	

	The filing also said a Politico Playbook report in September 2026, headlined “‘The vibes are very bad’ in Texas,” had “relied on unnamed sources to paint the Republican midterm convention in Dallas as a disaster.” According to the White House, citing a Breitbart News article that also attributed its reporting to anonymous sources, “Media reporting showed that the convention had over 100 million live stream views.”

schema.headline: Trump Rages at CNN’s Kaitlan Collins in Midnight Rant: She Has ‘Trump Addiction’

title: ‘Star Trek’ New York Comic-Con Panel to Feature William Shatner, ‘Starfleet Academy’ Season 2 Stars (EXCLUSIVE)
description: The “Star Trek” panel at New York Comic-Con will feature a special conversation with franchise legend William Shatner, Variety has learned exclusive
body:
The “Star Trek” panel at New York Comic-Con will feature a special conversation with franchise legend William Shatner, Variety has learned exclusively. 

	Shatner’s appearance comes as “Star Trek” is celebrating its 60th anniversary this year. He famously played Capt. James T. Kirk in “Star Trek: TOS” for three seasons as well as “Star Trek: The Animated Series” for another two. He and his fellow original series cast members then starred in six “Star Trek” films, while Shatner also appeared in the “Next Generation” film “Star Trek: Generations” alongside Patrick Stewart. 
	

	As previously announced, the panel will take place Oct. 10 from 3:15-4:15 pm ET on the Empire Stage and will offer fans a sneak preview of “Star Trek: Starfleet Academy” Season 2. Additional panelists will include “Starfleet Academy” stars Holly Hunter, Sandro Rosta, Bella Shepard, Karim Diané, and Robert Picardo, as well as co-showrunners and executive producers Alex Kurtzman and Noga Landau. 


	“Starfleet Academy” Season 2 does not yet have a premiere date, though it is slated to debut in 2027. As Variety exclusively reported in March, Season 2 will be the show’s final season. 

	The logline for “Starfleet Academy” Season 2 states that it “follows our cadets into their second year aboard the USS Athena. There, their ideals of leadership, friendship, romance and morality are put to the test as they navigate budding rivalries, shaky diplomatic negotiations, a fiercely competitive schoolwide tournament, and the arrival of a mysterious new cadet whose existence raises questions that could have consequences far beyond the classroom.” 
	

	The future of the “Star Trek” franchise remains uncertain beyond “Starfleet Academy” and the upcoming fifth and final season of “Star Trek: Strange New Worlds.” At the time of this publishing, no new shows have been announced, though Paramount is said to be keen on developing a new “Star Trek” film.

schema.headline: ‘Star Trek’ New York Comic-Con Panel to Feature William Shatner, ‘Starfleet Academy’ Season 2 Stars (EXCLUSIVE)

title: ‘Brace Your Heart’ Review: Tradition and Modernity Collide in an Impassioned Ode to Sámi Womanhood
description: For those of us who only ever think about reindeer when December draws in, and even then in a fairly abstract sense, “Brace Your Heart” arrives as a
body:
For those of us who only ever think about reindeer when December draws in, and even then in a fairly abstract sense, “Brace Your Heart” arrives as a flinty reality check. Following the life and trials of a young female reindeer herder in the present day, it’s stripped of any fairytale essence, and doesn’t stint on the grueling physical and economic challenges of the profession, even before the ugly actuality of being a woman in this male-dominated realm is made clear. The third feature from Swedish writer-director Amanda Kernell follows on from her 2016 debut “Sámi Blood” in spotlighting the experience of the indigenous Sámi community in northernmost Europe, to which Kernell herself belongs; where that film was a period piece, powerfully examining Sweden’s colonial oppression of her people, the filmmaker’s latest is a testament to the resilience of Sámi identity (and womanhood, in particular) in the 21st century.
	

	After premiering in Toronto’s Oscar-qualifying Platform program — where it received a special mention from the jury — “Brace Your Heart” had its European premiere in the main competition at San Sebastian: a festival one-two that indicates the film’s fairly broad arthouse appeal, despite its remote and little-known milieu. After “Sámi Blood” and Kernell’s 2020 sophomore feature “Charter” achieved solid international distribution, this rousing, accessible new work should follow suit — though given its youthful focus, specialist streaming may connect the film with its optimal audience.


	Much like “Sámi Blood,” which rested heavily on the charisma of novice actress and Sámi reindeer herder Lene Cecilia Sparrok, “Brace Your Heart” unearths a raw new talent in Elli Sara Valkeapää, also a herder, who handles an emotionally demanding role with impressive subtlety and stoicism. She plays Ejva, the 20-year-old daughter of a reindeer herder who’s suddenly thrust into her father’s shoes following his untimely death. Handed the literal reins to the family business, she’s forced to adapt fast to a tough line of work that takes an extreme toll on the body and mind — and that’s without such calamities as her snowmobile falling through thin ice into the freezing waters below. Kernell and DP Sophia Olsson shoot that heart-in-mouth setpiece with a kind of detached calm, as if to stress it’s just another bad day at the office.
	

	Though Ejva is strong and capable and has the proud support of her family, she’s still overwhelmed by the demands of going it alone — and so she strategically seeks an ally in Heaika (Andte Gaup-Juuso), a jockish local herding bigwig who has also been putting the moves on her romantically. Following her head more than her heart, she humors those too, despite being considerably more attracted to his gentler cousin Nejla (Vincent Niia), the man who rescued her from the aforementioned ice plunge. Framing this story of female agency and leadership as a conventional love triangle initially seems an oddly old-fashioned choice — though when Heaika’s behavior takes a startlingly toxic turn, “Brace Your Heart” expands into a study of contrasting schools of Sámi masculinity. And when Ejva turns to the conveniences of modern, urban life, she wonders if the effort of maintaining her familial and cultural legacy is worth it.

	If Kernell’s screenplay can feel a bit schematic in its funneling of wider social issues into the small, hard story of one individual, “Brace Your Heart” is otherwise played with pleasing, powerful restraint — beginning with Valkeapää’s quietly expressive performance of a naturally taciturn character. Often shot in tight closeups that expose the harsh impact of the climate on her features, she’s frequently given the luxury of time to think on screen, particularly when weighing up crucial decisions on which the future and reputation of her entire family may depend. 

	Kernell herself is a patiently observant filmmaker: Olsson’s camera isn’t blind to the pale, spectacular sweep of the surroundings, but takes a pragmatic, quasi-documentary approach to the action at hand. A hint of ethereal whimsy, albeit still couched in cultural authenticity, is provided by the breathy a capella swoops and stutters of Rebekka Karijord and Kristian Eidnes Andersen’s score. Shot with a largely non-professional cast in the extraordinary, unyielding landscape of the Sápmi region, “Brace Your Heart” offers a detailed window into the Sámi way of life, even outside the strictures of the script.

schema.headline: ‘Brace Your Heart’ Review: Tradition and Modernity Collide in an Impassioned Ode to Sámi Womanhood

title: ‘Today’ Snares Top Two Positions in Morning-News Battle for First Time in 14 Years
description:
NBC’s “Today” is back on top in TV’s never-ending morning wars.

	The A.M. news franchise finished the 2025-26 broadcast season with the most viewer
body:
NBC’s “Today” is back on top in TV’s never-ending morning wars.

	The A.M. news franchise finished the 2025-26 broadcast season with the most viewers overall among morning programs and the most viewers between the ages of 25 and 54, the demographic most coveted by advertisers in TV-news content. It is the first time since the 2011-2012 TV season, when Matt Lauer and Ann Curry served as co-anchors of the show, that “Today” has beaten its competitors on both categories.
	

	The wins come amid a trying period for show personnel. The kidnapping of Nancy Guthrie, mother of Savannah Guthrie, captured national attention during the first half of the year. The loss the Guthrie family continues to feel — Nancy Guthrie’s whereabouts remain unknown — continues to be discussed occasionally on air.


	“Today” captured an average of 2.938 million viewers for the season, 4%, or 114,000 viewers higher, than audience levels at ABC’s “Good Morning America,” according to data from Nielsen, and 67%, or 1.174 million higher than viewership at “CBS Mornings.” Overall, the audience for “Today” rose by 7%, or 185,000 viewers, over the previous season.

	“Today” won an average of 609,000 viewers between 25 and 54, 28%, or 134,000 more than “GMA” and 120%, or 332,000 more than “CBS Mornings.” It is the largest share of the demographic captured by the show in 15 years, according to data from Nielsen.

	One ever-present dynamic of TV’s morning-news battle is that it never ends. “Today” will have to contend with not only its usual competition from “GMA,” but a new lineup at CBS, where Norah O’Donnell has rejoined the network’s A.M. team.

schema.headline: ‘Today’ Snares Top Two Positions in Morning-News Battle for First Time in 14 Years

title: Disney+ and Hulu Raise Prices Again, the Fourth Hike in Four Years
description:
The streamflation trend continues: Disney is once again asking Disney+ and Hulu subscribers to pay even more for the streaming service.

	Disney+ Pr
body:
The streamflation trend continues: Disney is once again asking Disney+ and Hulu subscribers to pay even more for the streaming service.

	Disney+ Premium and Hulu Premium, the plans without ads, are both increasing from $18.99 to $21.49/month, up 13%. The pricing strategy is clearly aimed at pushing consumers toward bundles: The Disney+/Hulu Premium bundle is ticking up two bucks, from $19.99 to $21.99/month, which is nearly half what it would cost if you bought them separately.
	

	The ad-supported Disney+ and Hulu (SVOD only) plans are also getting a hike, from $11.99 to $12.49/month. The Disney+ and Hulu (with ads) remains unchanged at $12.99/month — just 50 cents more than each of the services if purchased separately.


	The Disney+ and Hulu price increases are effective Wednesday (Sept. 23) for new subscribers. Existing customers will see the new pricing on their next monthly bill.

	The higher prices come as Pixar blockbuster “Toy Story 5” debuted on Disney+ on Wednesday. Variety has reached out to Disney for additional info.

	Meanwhile, Disney also recently raised the price of the ESPN Unlimited service, which increased from $29.99 to $31.99/month effective Sept. 17.

	Disney’s streaming price hikes have become an annual ritual. The latest increases mark the fourth time in four years the Mouse House is raising rates in the U.S., after price hikes for Disney+ and Hulu in October 2024 and in October 2023.

	The ad-free Disney+ tier has now nearly doubled in price from the $10.99/month rate in 2023 prior to the fall increase that year.

	RELATED: Streaming Prices Continue to Balloon: Is ‘Streamflation’ at a Breaking Point?

schema.headline: Disney+ and Hulu Raise Prices Again, the Fourth Hike in Four Years

title: YouTube Locks Down Coachella Rights Through 2030 as It Unveils New Microdrama-Inspired Experience for Shorts, AI-Powered Tools for Music and Studio and More
description:
YouTube‘s staying in the Coachella desert for a few more years.

	The streamer will remain the exclusive free streaming home of Coachella through 20
body:
YouTube‘s staying in the Coachella desert for a few more years.

	The streamer will remain the exclusive free streaming home of Coachella through 2030, continuing its nearly 15-year partnership with the festival’s parent company Goldenvoice. The extension comes nearly six months after YouTube broadcast the Sabrina Carpenter, Justin Bieber, and Karol G-led edition of the festival, which became the platform’s most-watched Coachella livestream ever.
	

	“We’re excited to bring the energy of the desert to millions of music fans around the world,” YouTube CEO Neal Mohan said Wednesday during the company’s “Made on YouTube” event, where he unveiled the extension.


	During the event, the company introduced a suite of new features and tools for viewers and creators across its mediums. Some of its other new products include new custom feeds, AI-powered conversational functions across its YouTube and YouTube Music and new comment features, among many others.

	One significant launch: expanding shows to YouTube Shorts, allowing creators to format short-form videos into a structured experience with episodes laid out for viewers — or, in other words, format Shorts as microdramas. 

	YouTube said microdrama viewership surpassed 6.5 billion views in the first half of 2026, growing by more than 60% year-over-year, while microdrama viewership on TV screens increased by 90% year-over-year in 2026’s first half. Expanding Shorts into episode-like structures taps into the platform’s burgeoning living room audience, more than 35% of which watched YouTube Shorts on TV in July.
	

	“Shorts are more than a discovery engine to drive views to your longer videos, and viewers are not only watching them on mobile; they’re also watching them together on the biggest screen in their house,” Emily Moxley, YouTube’s vice president for product management for viewer AI, said on stage. “They’ve become a content genre all on their own.”

	The company is also infusing many of its products with AI. The company’s new “Ask” feature, available across YouTube and YouTube Music, allows users to pose queries to an AI agent for things like shoppable items featured in videos, new music recommendations and carrying conversations across different YouTube pages. The “Ask” features will begin rolling out later this year.

	For podcasts, the company is rolling out a “podcast lineup” feature within YouTube Music. The AI-driven tool allows users to get a spoken preview of shows and features an AI agent pressing users on why they like specific podcasts before pushing episodes to them. The tool begins testing later this year.

	The YouTube Music features were demoed by music creator Derrick Gee, who used the “Ask“ feature to dive deeper into Troye Sivan‘s single “She’s the Best” and the influences behind the track. Sivan himself, who got his start on YouTube, came out for an interview with Gee to discuss the platform’s impact on his career.

	“I uploaded my first YouTube video in 2007,” he said.  “I was a child, and it really still informs everything that I do. I would say to this day, because I learnt really, really early on that it was all about creating community and having such [a] direct line to people, and realizing that people are smart and people know and can feel when something is genuine.”

	For users, new features will appear right on their YouTube homepage. For its “custom feed” feature, which appears to be powered by AI, YouTube watchers can create new channels dedicated to recommended videos on topics they request to see, with the feeds remaining on their homepage. The feature was demoed during the event by fashion creator Mina Le, who showcased the in-the-works feature by feeds on stationary videos and “late night coziness” clips focused on ambient noises.

	“No clutter, no searching every time I want to dive in. Just this personal space curated for me that I can come back to whenever I want,” she said. “This new feature is a huge shift in the viewer experience of YouTube, a shift towards greater customization.”
	

	For creators who use its Studio suite, the company is rolling out another “Ask” feature to help creators edit and test out videos more easily, including by providing feedback. Other features include A/B testing for videos, letting the platform generate titles and thumbnails based on a creator’s style, dynamic thumbnails for different audiences and specific insights into video performance.

	The company is also rolling out new ways for creators to monetize their work, including a new “Hype with Jewels” feature that allows viewers to celebrate their favorite creators’ work. YouTube is also boosting its affiliate program globally so creators can earn more from affiliate links and brand partnerships form their fans.

	“Let’s face it, creators are the new global storefront, and your viewers are already lined up at the register,” Mary Ellen Coe, YouTube’s chief business officer, said on stage.

schema.headline: YouTube Locks Down Coachella Rights Through 2030 as It Unveils New Microdrama-Inspired Experience for Shorts, AI-Powered Tools for Music and Studio and More

title: Netflix Orders Two New Seasons of ‘Chef’s Table,’ Devoted to ‘Desserts’ and ‘Icons’ (EXCLUSIVE)
description: Netflix has picked up two new standalone seasons of its long-running food series “Chef’s Table.” The streamer is set to unroll “Chef’s Table: Icons”
body:
Netflix has picked up two new standalone seasons of its long-running food series “Chef’s Table.” The streamer is set to unroll “Chef’s Table: Icons” and “Chef’s Table: Desserts,” and for the first time, creator David Gelb is also directing every episode of both seasons himself. It’s the first time he’s directed an entire run of “Chef’s Table” since the series first launched in 2015.

	Both seasons consist of four episodes; featured chefs will be announced at a later date. Production is currently underway on the series around the world. 
	

	In the case of “Chef’s Table: Icons,” the logline notes that the season “turns its lens on the chefs who didn’t just run great restaurants — they built institutions. Each redefined dining for their place and time, transforming singular vision into something enduring: a destination, a movement, a standard others measure themselves against. This season explores what it takes to reach the summit of the culinary world — and the discipline, reinvention and sheer will required to stay there.”


	As for “Chef’s Table: Desserts,” the season logline promises to spotlight “the world’s most inventive dessert chefs and the artistry, precision and imagination behind their craft. The season explores fresh perspectives on sweets and confectionery from around the globe.”

	This reps the first new installments of “Chef’s Table” since “Chef’s Table: Legends” aired in 2025. Previous standalone themed seasons include “Chef’s Table: France” (2016), “Chef’s Table: Pastry” (2018), “Chef’s Table: BBQ” (2020), “Chef’s Table: Pizza” (2022), “Chef’s Table: Noodles” (2024) and “Chef’s Table: Legends.”
	

	Producers promise a mix of returning and new chefs this season — particularly “Desserts,” which they said will “spotlight pastry and dessert chefs who have never been featured on television before.” Series creator, director and exec producer Gelb has made a name for himself in the documentary and culinary worlds over the years, including via his landmark 2011 doc “Jiro Dreams of Sushi.”

	“‘Chef’s Table’ has always been about more than food — it’s about the personal journey of the chefs who tell stories with their cuisine — the obsession, discipline and heart that goes into every night of service in their kitchens and dining rooms,” Gelb said in a statement. “For ‘Desserts’ and ‘Icons,’ these stories were so exciting to me that I decided to take the camera and direct all eight episodes myself, and I’ve found myself profoundly moved by the experience of filming on the most intimate level with these chefs. After 10 years, our filmmaking team continues to strive to elevate ‘Chef’s Table’ to an even higher level, just like our chefs do in their restaurants every day.”

	“Chef’s Table” comes from Boardwalk Pictures and David Gelb Films. Gelb, Andrew Fried, Brian McGinn and Dane Lillegard are executive producers.

schema.headline: Netflix Orders Two New Seasons of ‘Chef’s Table,’ Devoted to ‘Desserts’ and ‘Icons’ (EXCLUSIVE)

title: Tom Cruise Is the Last Great Movie Star Still Chasing His Oscar. Can He Overcome ‘Digger’ Reviews to Get Him There?
description:
Tom Cruise is going to divide us this year, and that might be the most interesting thing about his Oscar prospects for “Digger.”

	Depending on whic
body:
Tom Cruise is going to divide us this year, and that might be the most interesting thing about his Oscar prospects for “Digger.”

	Depending on which screening you walked out of, it’s either the bravest swing of his late career or a miscalculation dressed up as one. Critics are divided, and audiences will be too. Typically, that reaction is a problem, but with Cruise, it might be what his campaign needs.


	For the first time in a long time, he is starring in something the industry has to argue about rather than simply admire. Alejandro González Iñárritu’s “Digger” is not what people are expecting, and how audiences react (via box office and word-of-mouth) will be the ultimate test of his star power.
	

	Before the festivals began, I posed a question: How divisive (or bad) would “Digger” need to be for Tom Cruise to lose this season? Venice, Telluride and Toronto have come and gone and now we approach the moment of truth. But there’s a more interesting question percolating — what will a Cruise Oscar campaign ask the Academy to recognize?

	“Digger” stars Cruise as Digger Rockwell, a wealthy tycoon who must save the world when one of his oil rigs malfunctions and causes an environmental catastrophe across the planet. The film also includes Riz Ahmed, John Goodman, Sandra Hüller, Michael Stuhlbarg and Jesse Plemons. The social embargo that lifted on Sept. 22 was mixed, with many praising Cruise’s performance but coming down hard on the film’s ultimate execution.

	For the better part of two decades, Cruise has not presented as just a working actor. He has become a brand equivalent to Steven Spielberg, a symbol of moviemaking itself. His image is no longer attached to performances so much as to the theatrical experience, to physical risk, to movie-star mythology and to the idea that someone still wants to do it the old-fashioned way: make movies for a giant screen. He doesn’t need to explain himself because the moving pictures do the work — along with the smile, the running, the airplanes, the motorcycles and the impossible stunts.
	

	That’s what makes his Oscar journey unusual. Cruise is one of the last major movie stars of the 1990s whose competitive Oscar story remains unfinished. The Academy has already honored his contemporaries — Will Smith for “King Richard,” Leonardo DiCaprio for “The Revenant,” Tom Hanks twice, Julia Roberts for “Erin Brockovich.” That was a generation built around stars whose names were the selling point, and Cruise’s roughly $1.88 billion (adjusted for inflation) domestic grosses put him squarely in that company. Even as his career has come to be defined by a global kind of theatrical power, he’s still just a boy standing in front of the voters asking them to choose him.

	So what kind of movie has Cruise chosen for his latest attempt?



	

					Tom Cruise in “Digger”
									Warner Bros.
	



	For Iñárritu, “Digger” is a significant swing coming off “Bardo,” which was pummeled by critics. This project feels like an attempt to reach back toward “Birdman” territory, when critics and audiences were in step with him. Iñárritu doesn’t seem to be simply directing a star synonymous with spectacle but dropping him into a film that is decidedly actor driven, one with auteurist ambitions. That’s something we haven’t seen from Cruise since teaming with Paul Thomas Anderson for 1999’s “Magnolia.”

	I respect the swing. Cruise and John Goodman are both delivering stellar work and could find themselves within arm’s length of nominations. I found Sophie Wilde to be the best in show, bringing a performance that lingers after the argument about everything else around her dies down.

	The superb Goodman is as he has been for decades — one of those dependable veteran actors still waiting on a first invitation to the dance. With comical and genre-varying triumphs like “Barton Fink,” “The Big Lebowski,” “Inside Llewyn Davis” and “Argo,” he’s still got it. If voters want a reason to finally recognize him, “Digger” gives them one. Riz Ahmed occupies what feels like the Philip Seymour Hoffman space — a presence that elevates whatever he’s in, even in a contained part. Sandra Hüller, meanwhile, is having a remarkable four-movie year, but “Digger” gives her less to work with than “Fatherland,” “Rose” or “Project Hail Mary” — the least likely of the four to land a nomination.
	

	On the technical side, the opportunities are clearer. Emmanuel “Chivo” Lubezki behind the camera is reason enough to sit up, and we’ve missed him; that puts cinematography and production design well within reach, with makeup and hairstyling undoubtedly in the conversation. That will help reinforce the movie as a filmmaking experience, and not as only a Cruise vehicle.

	Cruise’s most significant Oscar swing in years is a movie that asks audiences to take a position, and that’s a much riskier way to campaign for a statue. 

	As we look at his filmography and history with awards, we see a worthy career capper. He was nominated for an acting Oscar three times inside a 10-year stretch. He was the Vietnam veteran Ron Kovic in Oliver Stone’s “Born on the Fourth of July” (1989), a raw, furious turn that won him the Golden Globe and lost the Oscar to Daniel Day-Lewis (“My Left Foot”). He was the flailing sports agent in Cameron Crowe’s “Jerry Maguire” (1996), and lost to Geoffrey Rush (“Shine”). And then came his Frank T.J. Mackey, the predatory guru in Paul Thomas Anderson’s “Magnolia” (1999), a supporting turn that seemed like it would be “the one” before losing out to Michael Caine, who walked away with a second statue for “The Cider House Rules.”

	The Cruise who chased those nominations was angling to work with the most demanding filmmakers alive: Stone, Anderson, Stanley Kubrick on “Eyes Wide Shut,” Michael Mann on “Collateral.” Then, sometime in the 2000s, a different Cruise took over, the star whose name alone could still fill a theater. He hung off the side of an airplane, climbed the Burj Khalifa and turned “Mission: Impossible” into a decades-long experiment in testing his own limits. 

	And when the theatrical business was seemingly on its deathbed during the pandemic, he dragged audiences back with “Top Gun: Maverick,” which earned him a best picture nomination as a producer — the closest he’d come to the Oscar stage in years (but without an acting nomination).

	That’s what is at the center of this season. The very thing that makes Cruise the “last great movie star” may be what has kept the Oscar from him. Spectacle doesn’t usually win acting trophies, and neither does sincerity in service of a franchise. The Academy rewards the side of Cruise’s career he left behind, and he left it behind because the other lane needed him more. He stopped needing the Academy — until that became the one thing box office couldn’t buy.
	



	

					“Digger”
									©Warner Bros/Courtesy Everett Collection
	



	The Academy has already given Cruise an Oscar of sorts. Last year, it bestowed him with an honorary award, the industry’s way of acknowledging what he has meant to the movies. It’s a gesture of respect, but it can carry a different message: We know we never gave you the competitive one, so here’s the gold so the town can close this chapter. That doesn’t mean he will automatically lose. Paul Newman took an honorary Oscar in 1986, the Academy’s nod to a career full of competitive losses and he won the competitive best actor prize the very next year for “The Color of Money.” And the film that finally handed Newman his statuette happened alongside his then 24-year-old co-star Tom Cruise.

	“Digger” is Cruise refusing to let his own chapter close. A consensus crowd-pleaser would have made the narrative easy. Instead, Cruise has made something that people will be talking about (good and bad).

	The performance has to survive the argument to matter. If it does, the story will write itself. If it doesn’t, the honorary award will look like the right way to recognize the career at exactly the right moment.

	The question “Digger” raises is whether it reads as dramatic rather than physical. He has spent years as the safest bet an audience can place. If you put Tom Cruise in the movie, he’ll deliver. But now he’s asking voters to take a different kind of chance on him.

	The question was never whether Tom Cruise deserves to be celebrated. He already is. The question is whether, after years of embodying movie stardom, he can make voters look past the symbol and see the actor again. So what does an Oscar season look like with the last movie star still chasing the one prize that has eluded him? It looks complicated.

schema.headline: Tom Cruise Is the Last Great Movie Star Still Chasing His Oscar. Can He Overcome ‘Digger’ Reviews to Get Him There?

title: Mitch McConnell Smiles, Gives Peace Sign As He Arrives Home
description:
Mitch McConnell
                          Everything's Groovy With Me!!!
body:
Mitch McConnell
                          Everything's Groovy With Me!!!

                              September 23, 2026
                            7:15 AM PDT
                                                                      |
                                                                Updated 
                                  September 23, 2026
                                7:55 AM PDT
                                    
      
    
        
                    
                  
      
    
            Mitch McConnell comes in peace ... he was all smiles as he arrived home after a hard day's work on Capitol Hill ... and video shows the Senator in great spirits.
      
    
            After three hours of work in the Senate, the Kentucky lawmaker returned to his D.C. home Tuesday evening ... and he flashed a peace sign as he was wheeled inside.
      
    
            Mitch was in a wheelchair ... with four people helping him.
      

            The sighting came after Mitch voted for a cloture motion to end the debate on a district judge's nomination ... but it fell short of the 60 votes needed.
      
    
        
                    
                  
      
    
            Mitch resurfaced last week after disappearing from public view for three months following a bad fall in June, which required a hospital stay and a rehab stint.
      
    
            He says his recovery "has been a long and often frustrating process, and the lingering effects of childhood polio haven't made it any easier."

title: Texas Rangers Seeking Evidence Of Manslaughter Related to Camp Mystic Flood Deaths
description:
Camp Mystic Flood Deaths
                          Texas Rangers Seeking Evidence Of Manslaughter
body:
Camp Mystic Flood Deaths
                          Texas Rangers Seeking Evidence Of Manslaughter
                      
                  
                                                                        Published 
                              September 23, 2026
                            6:58 AM PDT
                                                                            
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Camp Mystic is facing a criminal investigation ... and investigators say they are on the hunt for evidence of manslaughter and homicide after 28 people died there last year in a flood.
      
    
            Texas Rangers have applied for search warrants to obtain electronic communications from the camp's owners, who have not been charged with a crime ... according to multiple reports.
      
    
            Officials say these communications may contain evidence of crimes ... including manslaughter, negligent homicide, and child abandonment.
      

            Texas Ranger Brant Johnston painted a grim picture of the camp's preparedness for the floods, writing in an affidavit that the camp's emergency plans were not sufficient, that there were not enough counselors for each cabin, and that emergency drills were not conducted.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Johnston added ... "Camp Mystic, LLC was aware of and consciously disregarded a substantial and unjustifiable risk of death to the campers in their care."
      
    
            In the face of the latest legal bombshell, the camp still has plans to reopen its doors next year ... despite 28 people -- including 25 young girls, two teen counselors and the camp director -- dying during last year's fatal flooding.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            In a July filing submitted as part of the camp's bankruptcy case ... the camp's proposed chief restructuring officer told the court they have more than $1 million from prospective campers for a future season.
      
    
            The filing asked the court to let Camp Mystic keep using its standard cash management system to keep operations running smoothly as it began the bankruptcy process.

            A woman says she was trapped next to a guy who was pleasuring himself aboard a United Airlines flight ... and, so far, the man has gotten off scot-free.
      
    
            The 25-year-old woman told NBC News she was seated next to the man on a flight from Rochester, New York, to Newark Liberty International Airport in New Jersey on September 3 when things suddenly got X-rated.
      
    
            She said the "unassuming" and "pretty normal looking" 35-to-40-year-old man started masturbating right in front of her ... all while staring at her.
      

                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            The woman told NBC ... "I just got the sense [he] had done it before ... People don't just do those things at 6 AM."
      
    
            She said she promptly reported the incident to flight staff, who allowed her to leave her seat until it was time to land. The plane was full, so she had to stand in the aisle to get away from the alleged masturbator.
      
    
            The woman also said flight attendants promised her she would only have to sit next to the dude for about 5 minutes until they landed ... but it turned out to be a lot longer.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Even worse, the woman said once they landed, the man exited the plane and disappeared without facing the music.
      
    
            She said United Airlines provided her with a measly $100 flight credit ... even though the total cost of her trip was $400. 
      
    
            A rep for United Airlines tells TMZ ... the airline is "looking into this report," but would not say if law enforcement was notified.

Bernie Sanders

                            6:30 AM PDT
                                                                            
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                                  
      
    
            Bernie Sanders is asking Congress to act fast on the dangers of A.I. ... introducing a bill that would ban artificial superintelligence.
      
    
            The Senator from Vermont and Rep. Greg Casar are unveiling legislation today that would create a new federal agency to oversee advanced A.I. ... this according to AP.
      
    
            Bernie told the Associated Press ... "It doesn't take a genius to say, 'slow it down' ... Do we really want to develop a super intelligence that when it becomes smarter than human beings could act independently of human control? I don't think we do."
      

        
                    
                  
      
    
            The senator -- who previously told TMZ he wants both China and the U.S. to ban A.I.'s superintelligence -- has previously spoken out about wanting to slow down the new tech's accelerated advancements.
      
    
            Bernie's announcement comes just days after President Donald Trump announced his own solution to the mounting concern -- an A.I. Force.
      
    
            Despite Trump's calling the concern around A.I. a "hoax," several members of the tech community have sounded the alarm on a potential A.I.-driven apocalypse if its capabilities aren't kept in check.
      
    
            Bernie's bill would pause advanced A.I. development until the guardrails are put in place ... and folks at the top A.I. companies are said to be endorsing the bill.

title: 'Amazing Race' Contestant Tim Janus Dead at 49
description:
'Amazing Race' Competitor
                          Tim Janus Dead At 49
body:
'Amazing Race' Competitor
                          Tim Janus Dead At 49
                      
                  
                                                                        Published 
                              September 23, 2026
                            7:20 AM PDT
                                                                            
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Former "Amazing Race" contestant Tim Janus, who competed alongside Joey Chestnut on the show's 30th season, is dead.
      
    
            Tim, who was known in the competitive eating circuit as Eater X, died Sept. 16 following a cancer diagnosis ... his publicist confirmed to Major League Eating.
      
    
            He climbed the sport's ranks to eventually become the No. 2 competitive eater in the world ... behind only Joey.
      

            Tim was once crowned the world ramen eating champion after tucking away 10.5 pounds in just under 8 minutes.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            In addition to his ramen-eating dominance ... he also became the nigiri world eating champion.
      
    
            Tim competed in the famous Nathan's Hot Dog Eating Contest on the Fourth of July in 2014 ... downing 44 hot dogs.
      
    
            No stranger to TV, Janus took home $1,600 on "Cash Cab" and also competed on the syndicated version of "Who Wants to Be a Millionaire" ... winning $100,000.
      
    
            He is survived by his mother, father, and sister.
      
    
            Tim was 49.
